definition: The value $L$ that $f(x)$ gets closer and closer to as $x$ approaches $a$, written $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L$.
A straight line joining two points on a curve. It is also called a secant.
The straight line that touches a curve at a point and has the same gradient as the curve there.
The gradient function $f'(x)$, or $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$: the gradient of $y = f(x)$ at each $x$, and the rate of change of $y$ with respect to $x$.
